correctness.rationale: The SIC projectors form a real Hermitian basis with dual D_j=((d+1)P_j-I)/d. Erasing r,s gives exactly a two-dimensional Hermitian kernel. Trace-zero pure-state differences restrict it to multiples of P_r-P_s, whose rank and image force both states into the span of u_r,u_s. Equality of a single complex off-diagonal entry on that 2-space yields exhaustive singleton/reflected-doubleton fibers, including boundary cases. The p_r and p_s gap and chordal factor are exact identities. In dimensions d>=4 any rank<=2 Hermitian kernel element must be traceless; an explicit d=3 signature-(1,1) counterexample establishes the unknown-norm boundary. The saved Hesse-SIC checker verifies one finite example but is not used for arbitrary-d correctness.

value.rationale: The erasure threshold is a natural measurement-design invariant: one deleted probability is redundant because SIC effects sum to identity, whereas two create unavoidable pure-state ambiguity. The substantive result is an all-dimensional exact classification of **which** states fail and their complete two-point fibers, with an exact invisible-chordal-distance factor and a sharp dimension-dependent unknown-norm boundary, not merely the elementary count of measurements or an isolated pair of ambiguous vectors.
